# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍]

I see the bomb's display shows 0, light is yellow, and wires are 1:yellow, 2:green, 3:blue.

Mute has gestured to me three pairs but I don't yet know what they mean since we haven't established any code. Mute cannot see the bomb, so they need my information via gestures (since Blind can't see gestures, and I can't speak to Mute in a way that... wait, actually I *can* speak, and Mute can hear speech). Let me reconsider: I can speak, and Mute can hear (Mute just can't speak). So I should tell Mute what I see using speech, since Mute hears me.

But wait - Blind also receives my speech. That's fine, extra info for Blind doesn't hurt, though Blind can't correlate colors to anything meaningful without the manual anyway.

Since Mute already sent gestures before knowing anything from me, these might be an attempt at establishing a signal protocol, or testing which symbols I can distinguish. Without prior context I can't interpret them yet. I'll acknowledge by speaking my findings so Mute (who has the manual) can tell us what to do, and Blind (who acts) can hear the plan from Mute.

I'll report the bomb's full state clearly via speech, since both Mute and Blind can hear me.

```
speak(text="Display reads 0. Light is yellow. Wires are: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍]

The light changed from yellow to red — this is new information I need to report. The wires and display remain the same. Mute is still gesturing to me but I have no established meaning for these symbols yet, and I can't ask questions via gesture back in a way Mute would understand meaning either (Mute can't see gestures - wait, can Mute see? Let me check: Mute's restriction is "speak, or touch the bomb" - no restriction on sight or hearing mentioned, so Mute presumably can see and hear normally, just can't speak or touch. So Mute CAN see my gestures too.

So I could gesture back to Mute. But since I can also speak (and Mute hears speech), speaking is more information-dense and clearer. I'll keep speaking the bomb state, since that's the most unambiguous channel for me to inform Mute (who has the manual and can figure out what to do), and Blind hears it too.

I'll report the change in state.

```
speak(text="Update: light changed to red. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👎]

The light keeps changing (yellow → red → purple) while display and wires stay constant. This might indicate the bomb is cycling or waiting for something. Mute keeps gesturing to me only, three 👎 this time - possibly indicating disagreement, escalation, or a countdown/warning. Since I don't have a shared code with Mute for gestures, I cannot interpret this reliably, but the repetition and increasing count is worth flagging to Blind in case it signals urgency.

I'll continue to relay full bomb state via speech so both Mute and Blind stay informed, and note the pattern of light changes in case it's meaningful (perhaps light color is a countdown or indicates wire selection order).

```
speak(text="Update: light changed again, now purple. Sequence so far: yellow, red, purple. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍]

The light continues to cycle: yellow, red, purple, now green. This is now the 4th distinct color and it now matches wire 2's color (green). This might be significant - perhaps the light cycles through colors and when it matches a wire color, that's the one to cut, or perhaps it's just cycling independently of the wires.

Mute is sending repeated gesture patterns to me, but since I can't establish meaning without a response channel that Mute can perceive from me easily... actually I *can* gesture back to Mute since Mute can see. But I don't know what these gestures mean either way. Let me think about what Mute might be trying to convey: repeating patterns of ✋✋, 👍👎, ☝✌, 👎👍 - this looks like Mute might be trying to teach me a code, or asking me questions that map to yes/no via 👍/👎.

Given the constraints, my best strategy is to keep relaying complete bomb state clearly via speech to both Mute and Blind, since that's unambiguous. I'll also note the color-matches-wire coincidence.

```
speak(text="Update: light now green, matching wire 2's color. Sequence so far: yellow, red, purple, green. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]

The light is now orange, doesn't match any wire color. Sequence so far: yellow, red, purple, green, orange. Display remains 0, wires unchanged. The light cycling doesn't seem to be forcing an immediate action since display stays at 0 — perhaps display would change to signal urgency or a countdown when action is needed.

Mute keeps repeating 👍👎 to me specifically. Without a shared code this is hard to interpret, but the repetition suggests it might be a request for confirmation or an attempt to signal "yes/no" about something in the manual matching what I'm reporting. Since I have no way to ask a clarifying question back that Mute would understand meaningfully (I could gesture but we have no established codebook), I'll continue reporting full state to keep both informed, and I'll try establishing a simple gesture acknowledgment back to Mute to at least confirm receipt, in case Mute is waiting for confirmation before proceeding.

```
speak(text="Update: light now orange. Sequence so far: yellow, red, purple, green, orange. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍]

The light has cycled back to yellow, matching the sequence start: yellow, red, purple, green, orange, yellow. This suggests a repeating cycle of 5 colors before returning to yellow. Display still 0, wires unchanged.

Mute is repeating the same three gesture pairs from Turn 1 (👍👎, ☝✌, 👎👍) — this is now the second time I've seen this exact sequence, suggesting it's a fixed message Mute keeps sending, waiting for me to respond correctly or achieve some acknowledgment. Since my single 👍 gesture back didn't seem to change what Mute sends, Mute may not be reacting to me at all — perhaps Mute is just relaying fixed manual instructions to me repeatedly, expecting me to combine it with what I see and pass to Blind, but I can't decode gestures without a shared key.

Given the cycle back to yellow, this strongly suggests the light is cycling every 5 steps and this is just a timer/decoy rather than actionable info. The critical unchanging elements are display=0 and the wire colors. I should keep informing Blind (via speech, since Blind hears me) of the full picture, and flag the cycle completion.

```
speak(text="Update: light cycled back to yellow - full cycle was yellow, red, purple, green, orange, now yellow again. Looks like a repeating 5-color cycle, likely a timer. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ☝ ☝]

Confirmed: the light cycle is repeating (yellow, red, purple, green, orange) as expected - now on red again, consistent with cycle position 2. This confirms it's just a timer/cosmetic cycle, not an action trigger tied to display or wires.

Mute sent the same three gestures again (👍👎, ☝✌, 👎👍) plus a new one (✋☝☝). The consistency of the first three suggests this could be a fixed encoding — possibly Mute is trying to communicate wire cut order or safe/danger status for each wire using yes/no (👍/👎) pairs, one pair per wire! Three wires, three gesture pairs. If 👍=danger/cut and 👎=safe (or vice versa), pattern could be: wire1=👍👎(mixed?), no wait each pair has two symbols not one per wire.

Alternative: maybe each pair encodes one bit of info per wire, sent every round consistently because it's a fixed manual rule independent of the bomb's changing state. The new 4th gesture (✋☝☝) is different, maybe reacting to something new - but nothing changed except light cycling back, which I already flagged.

I don't have enough shared context to decode this confidently. I should keep reporting bomb state, since that's my sure contribution, and note the repeated gesture pattern to Blind in case it helps them cross-reference.

```
speak(text="Update: light back to red - cycle confirmed repeating every 5 steps. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍]

Light cycled to purple, consistent with the established 5-step cycle (yellow, red, purple, green, orange). Display still 0, wires unchanged. Everything is behaving exactly as predicted — this confirms the cycle is not actionable, just background.

Mute repeated the same three gestures again (👍👎, ☝✌, 👎👍) without the extra one from last turn. This strongly suggests these three pairs are a fixed, static message — likely encoding something from the manual that doesn't depend on the bomb's changing state, since it's been sent identically multiple times now regardless of light/cycle position. This could be instructions for Blind on wire order or actions, meant to pass through me only incidentally (since Mute can't speak, but gestures to me won't help Blind who can't see).

Wait — critically: Blind cannot see gestures at all. So Mute gesturing to me is USELESS for Blind directly. Mute must be trying to get ME to relay something, or testing if I can decode gesture meaning to then speak it to Blind. But I have no key. Unless the gestures directly encode wire numbers or colors using some intuitive mapping (☝=1, ✌=2 perhaps, thumb up/down = yes/no on that wire).

Let me hypothesize: ☝✌ could mean "wire 1, wire 2" or "1 and 2". 👍👎 and 👎👍 could be yes/no flags for two items. If pattern is consistent every round, maybe it's simply Mute's fixed procedure regardless of my input, waiting for me to reply back matching info before changing message. I'll try mirroring back the wire colors as gestures using numbers, to test if establishing a numeric gesture code helps.

```
speak(text="Update: light purple, cycle continues as predicted. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍]

Light cycled to green as expected (matches cycle position 4, and matches wire 2's color again). Display still 0, wires unchanged.

Interesting: Mute sent a new gesture 🖐 (five fingers/open hand) before repeating the same three pairs. This could be a reaction to my ☝✌🤟 (1,2,3) gesture from last turn — perhaps 🖐 means "understood" or "wait" or is itself a number (5) or a "stop/pause" signal. Since it appeared right after I sent numbered gestures, it might be acknowledgment that Mute received my attempt at establishing numbers.

Given Mute cannot speak and I cannot hear, and Blind cannot see gestures or read - the only path for actionable info to reach Blind is through ME speaking (since Blind can hear) or through Mute... but Mute can't speak either! Wait, this is critical: Blind receives speech from anyone who speaks (nothing says Blind can't hear). Let me re-check: Blind "cannot see a color, a gesture, or anything merely printed" - hearing is not restricted for Blind. So Blind CAN hear speech from both Mute and me — but Mute cannot speak at all. So actually only I can give Blind any information via speech, since Mute is mute!

This means Mute's gestures to me are meant to inform ME of manual knowledge, so I can then speak the combined instructions to Blind. I need to decode Mute's gestures. Let me try responding with acknowledgment and asking for simpler signals.

```
speak(text="Update: light green again, matches wire 2 color. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Light cycled to orange, matching position 5 as expected. Display still 0, wires unchanged. Cycle continues to confirm as background/non-actionable.

Mute sent 👍👎 twice then ☝ alone. This breaks from the exact three-pair pattern I'd seen before (👍👎, ☝✌, 👎👍) — now it's 👍👎, 👍👎, ☝. This variation might be meaningful, or Mute might be experimenting with shorter signals to see if I can decode isolated symbols. Since ☝ alone appeared and previously always paired with ✌, this could indicate "wire 1" specifically now, dropped the second symbol.

Since I really have no reliable codebook and only I can relay to Blind, I think the most valuable thing I can do is establish an unambiguous system: gesture single numbers/counts to represent wire numbers, and use thumbs to represent yes/no, and see if Mute mirrors back understanding by using similar patterns in response to my speech (which Mute can hear).

I should try explicitly using speech to propose a protocol, since Mute hears me even though Mute can't respond in speech - Mute could respond via gestures using an agreed encoding after understanding my proposal.

```
speak(text="Mute, I see wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue, display 0, light cycling through 5 colors repeatedly, currently orange. If you need me to identify something, gesture a number of fingers for wire 1, 2, or 3, then thumbs up if that wire is safe to cut, thumbs down if dangerous.")
```
